headline: South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Africa: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
- Western Russia: One dead and three injured in three Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
- Military Times, 8 hours ago: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
Sailors must maintain a ​state of alert and readiness, heightened in the case of the George Washington due to the threat of Iranian attacks.
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: US Army tests counter-drone tech at Mexican border as cartel drone use rises.
The service is seeking to sharpen its defenses against the growing threat of drone use by cartels.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
The Global Afrikan Congress (GAC) is demanding an apology from parliamentarian Everald Warmington for his “uninformed assertions” that Black Africans who sold people into the transatlantic slave trade should be held more accountable than Europeans buyers. In an open letter to Warmington, the GAC – an international Pan-African organisation of people of African descent across 35 countries – also urged the St Catherine South Western member of parliament (MP) to undertake necessary research to correct his “colonial miseducation”.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One dead and three injured in three Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: One dead and three injured in three Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk.
A woman was killed and three other people, including a 13-year-old boy, were injured as a result of three Russian airstrikes on the Sloviansk hromada in Donetsk Oblast on 5 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Six killed and 59 injured in Russian attack on Kharkiv – photos.
The attack has damaged residential buildings, cars, a warehouse and an industrial facility in Kharkiv’s Slobidskyi district; 30 people are still in hospital, including three in an extremely serious condition.
- Ukrainska Pravda, Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Russian drones attack Turkish vessel, captain killed – Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy says two Russian drones hit a Turkish-owned civilian vessel carrying maize in neutral waters, killing its captain.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian attack destroys Kusum pharmaceutical plant in Sumy.
A Kusum employee was killed when the company’s Sumy facility was destroyed on 4 October. The pharmaceutical firm is assessing the damage and says it will work to maintain uninterrupted medicine supplies.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
- Balkan Insight, 9 hours ago: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
MPs in first reading adopt major changes to law governing the Hague-based war crimes court following conviction of former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders – although enforcement requires second vote.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: Germany risks being drawn into ‘violent conflict’ with Russia, spy chief warns.
The head of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency also cautioned that NATO countries must beware of Moscow's "little green men."
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: From the rent crisis to Trump: 5 things that will shape Spain’s snap election.
Shifting attitudes toward the far right, fallout from the Ceuta crisis and the U.S. president's geopolitical maneuvers could have a major impact on the Nov. 29 vote.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Hungary’s New Government Haunted by Orban’s House of Terror.
The fate of Budapest’s House of Terror, a controversial museum which focuses on life under totalitarianism in the 20th century, could spark another round of the ‘culture war’.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
[Dabanga] Dilling, South Kordofan -- Four civilians, including a child and a woman, have been killed in RSF drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods in Dilling, South Kordofan, the Sudan Doctors Network says. The network condemns the attacks as a grave violation of international humanitarian law.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
Following almost two weeks of internal conflict that threatens a wider regional war in Ethiopia, the country's prime minister has vowed that government forces are ready to bring a rebel offensive under control.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan War - Fighting On Ethiopian Border, Drone Attacks On Ed Damazin.
[Dabanga] Ed Damazin -- The RSF-aligned Tasees Alliance forces announced on Saturday that they had taken full control of areas in Roseires locality, north-east of Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, after seizing several areas, including Menze, Jabal El Nimr, Jabal El Num, Basharkat, Matanguya, Mangaling El Jawani, Masnabiga, and Makala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's New Rebel War Redraws Alliances Across the Horn of Africa.
[RFI] Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Trump blames Democrats and Ukraine for soaring US fuel prices, not Iran war.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Trump blames Democrats and Ukraine for soaring US fuel prices, not Iran war.
Trump shifts blame for fuel price hikes to blue states like California and Ukraine strikes on Russian oil refineries.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Ukraine says Russian drone attack sinks ship in Romanian waters.
The latest suspected incursion on NATO's eastern flank increases fears that the war in Ukraine threatens to spill over.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Former hostage Emily Damari calls out denial, distortion of October 7, thanks British supporters.
"It was not an accident," Damari said in a video released on Monday. "It was a planned terrorist attack, in which innocent people were murdered, raped, injured, and kidnapped from their homes."
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Herzog says he told US Congress that terror 'undermines' regional peace three months before Oct. 7.
Herzog also addressed reports that Israeli security officials were unaware that the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 was barred from Oman Air amid concerns over his radicalization.
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Maybe People Facing Infertility Are Not the Problem - - We Are.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Maybe People Facing Infertility Are Not the Problem - - We Are.
[New Zimbabwe] A month ago, someone asked me to write about how to overcome the stigma of infertility, and as I reflected on that question, I realised that perhaps the couples and individuals facing infertility are not the issue, we are.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: Namibia: Making the Leap to University - Welcome to the Freedom Nobody Warned You About.
[Namibian] There is a certain excitement that comes with finishing high school. For years, you have been told where to be, when to submit your work, what subjects to take and, to some extent, what is expected of you. Then suddenly, university is waiting.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Times of India - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh. The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: At Moscow moot, Pakistan says terrorism remains core of Afghanistan's problems.
Pakistan’s Special Representative for Afghanistan Mohammad Sadiq on Monday said that terrorism remained at the core of Afghanistan’s problems, reaffirming that Pakistan would continue to take “all appropriate measures” for ensuring the safety of its citizens, in accordance with international law. Sadiq made these remarks at the eighth meeting of Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan in the Russian capital.
- The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: ‘Abandoned province’: Amir Muqam slams PTI, says not in favour of governor’s rule in KP but security risks persist.
Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam on Monday slammed the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, stressing that the federal government was not “in favour of governor’s rule” amid the party’s march, but warning of national security risks. The minister’s comments came as KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the party’s long march towards Islamabad on Sunday, saying that the party would “not accept” any policy against the interests of the people of KP. PTI went ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government.
India - bottom line: 'Attacked Thrice After Talks': Iran President Says US Dialogue 'Pointless'.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: 'Attacked Thrice After Talks': Iran President Says US Dialogue 'Pointless'.
The Middle East war was started in late February by the US and Israel when they launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, even as Washington and Tehran were in the midst of negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Trump says Ukraine strikes on Russia refinery, not Iran war, driving gas prices.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?.
Islamabad has not publicly acknowledged direct involvement in Saudi Arabia's offensive inside Yemen. However, several reports point that Pakistani forces could be helping Saudi Arabia shift more of its military resources towards the war by taking over defensive responsibilities inside the kingdom. That could allow Saudi forces to concentrate on the offensive against the Houthis without Pakistan formally becoming a combatant in Yemen.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: US Approves $1 Billion Weapons Sale To UAE As Gulf Faces Iran Drone Threat.
The Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System converts unguided rockets into precision munitions that can be employed for purposes including shooting down drones, thereby avoiding the use of costly missiles to shoot down comparatively cheap aircraft.
Asia - bottom line: US bombers moved from UK airbase due to Iran-linked threats, Trump says.
- South China Morning Post - China, NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: US bombers moved from UK airbase due to Iran-linked threats, Trump says.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that a threat linked to Iran ⁠had prompted the removal of American B-1 bombers from a British airbase. The planes had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the preferred European base for US bombers, and had recently been used in US strikes on Iran. Last week, five British men were arrested near the base – which Iran’s Revolutionary Guards previously said was a legitimate target – on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. “We had an idea that there might be a...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Former American Idol singer Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for wife’s murder.
A former Ohio music pastor who once appeared on American Idol was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole on Monday after a jury convicted him of murdering his wife while he was having an affair. Prosecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, staged a home invasion in February after shooting Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old teacher and volleyball coach. Flynn claimed she was killed by a burglar. With tears rolling down his cheeks, Flynn addressed the courtroom ahead of the sentencing and...
- South China Morning Post - China, NK News, 12 hours ago: Seoul probe reveals border mine blast caused by North Korea.
South Korea ⁠said on Monday that a ⁠recent border blast that seriously wounded two ⁠of its soldiers was caused by mines planted by North Korea. North Korea, which has been fortifying its border with South Korea since April 2024, deployed up to 7,000 workers to install mines and fences this year, with some 50 incidents of ‌crossing the border, according to a briefing on Monday by the South’s military. The two Koreas are still technically at war after their 1950-53 war ended in an armistice rather...
- South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: ‘There will be no Hamas rule in Gaza,’ Netanyahu vows at October 7 memorial.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group’s October 7, 2023 attack. Monday is a national day of remembrance for the deadliest day in Israel’s history, with flags lowered to half mast on public buildings from 6.29am, the time the attack began. Speaking during a state ceremony at the Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem, Netanyahu said “we have achieved enormous...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: North Korean, Taliban military officials hold talks at Russian war games.
- NK News, 15 hours ago: North Korean, Taliban military officials hold talks at Russian war games.
A North Korean military official met a Taliban counterpart on the sidelines of a Russian military exercise and weapons expo last week, where the DPRK joined Afghanistan and dozens of other countries as an observer. The Russian Defense Ministry announced Saturday that North Korea was among the 33 states that dispatched observers to its Center-2026 […]
- Yonhap News Agency, 6 hours ago: Ex-USFK commander warns time-based OPCON transfer could weaken deterrence against N. Korea.
WASHINGTON, Oct. 5 (Yonhap) -- A former commander of U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) wa...
- NK News, 13 hours ago: Trump reaffirms ‘great’ relation with Kim Jong Un and nuclear-armed states.
President Donald Trump on Saturday touted his relations with nuclear-armed nations, specifically North Korea, as the U.S. State Department reaffirmed his willingness to diplomatically engage with the DPRK. Speaking at a 2026 midterm election campaign rally in Ohio, Trump said he got “along great with Kim Jong Un” and that it was important to maintain […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Car destroyed in another suburban firebombing in Melbourne's north-west.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Car destroyed in another suburban firebombing in Melbourne's north-west.
A car has been destroyed in an arson attack in Keilor less than 24 hours after a firebombing in nearby Taylors Hill.
- The Guardian - Australia, 9 hours ago: Australian leaders condemn pro-Palestine vigils planned for 7 October anniversary amid Jewish commemorations.
Peak Jewish bodies organise ceremonies on third anniversary of attacks that triggered conflict in which 74,000 Palestinians have been killed Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Jewish Australians will mark the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks on Wednesday as Labor state governments condemn pro-Palestinian vigils to be held the same day. Peak Jewish bodies have organised commemorations across the capital cities but avoided publicising locations as community members report ongoing fears for their safety since the Bondi terror attack in December.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: Morning Mail: Australians buried in unmarked graves; proposal to nationalise supermarkets; and revisiting Sandpapergate.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Morning everyone. Today, a Guardian Australia investigation reveals how impoverished Australians are being buried in unmarked communal graves, a practice described by grieving relatives as “unspeakable”.
- ABC News Australia, just now: Man in 20s dies after being stabbed in neck in North Albury.
A police strike force has been set up to investigate the death of a man found stabbed in North Albury last month.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
